result.topic_en: A theorem with proof giving a recurrence for the coefficients of the power $P^\lambda$ of a power series $P=1+x^\alpha+x^\beta+\dots$, with a corollary on representing numbers as sums of $\lambda$ terms of the exponent sequence.
result.transcription:
508 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Analysis.

107.

(N. Fuss.)

Theorema. Proposita serie potestatum quacunque
$$P = 1 + x^\alpha + x^\beta + x^\gamma + x^\delta + \text{etc.}$$
ejusque sumatur potestas exponentis $\lambda$, nempe $P^\lambda$, in qua evoluta occurrat terminus $[n]\,x^n$, ejus coëfficiens $[n]$ ita pendebit ab aliquibus praecedentium, ut sit
$$n\,[n] = {+\lambda\alpha \atop -(n-\alpha)}[n-\alpha] {+\lambda\beta \atop -(n-\beta)}[n-\beta] {+\lambda\gamma \atop -(n-\gamma)}[n-\gamma] {+ \atop -}{\text{etc.} \atop \text{etc.}}$$
quae expressio eousque est continuanda, quamdiu numeri $n-\alpha$, $n-\beta$, $n-\gamma$, etc. non fiunt negativi.

Demonstratio. Ponatur $P^\lambda = S$, erit $lS = \lambda lP$ et $\frac{dS}{S} = \frac{\lambda dP}{P}$, hincque $PdS = \lambda SdP$, quae aequalitas ita repraesentetur $P\,.\,\frac{xdS}{dx} = \lambda S\,.\,\frac{xdP}{dx}$. Cum igitur sit $P = 1 + x^\alpha + x^\beta + x^\gamma + \text{etc.}$ erit
$$\frac{xdP}{dx} = \alpha x^\alpha + \beta x^\beta + \gamma x^\gamma + \delta x^\delta + \text{etc.}$$
Jam in serie $S$ occurrat terminus $[n]\,x^n$, praeter quem considerentur eae potestates, quae per $\frac{xdP}{dx}$ multiplicatae producere possunt potestatem $x^n$, qui termini ita repraesententur
$$S = \ldots\ldots [n]\,x^n\,[n-\alpha]\,x^{n-\alpha}\,[n-\beta]\,x^{n-\beta} \text{ etc.}$$
Hinc ergo erit
$$\lambda S\frac{xdP}{dx} = \lambda\alpha[n-\alpha]\,x^n + \lambda\beta[n-\beta]\,x^n + \lambda\gamma[n-\gamma]\,x^n + \text{etc.}$$
Deinde cum ex iisdem terminis sit
$$\frac{xdS}{dx} = n\,[n]\,x^n + (n-\alpha)[n-\alpha]\,x^{n-\alpha} + (n-\beta)[n-\beta]\,x^{n-\beta} + \text{etc.}$$
quae in $P$ ducta, pro potestate $x^n$ praebet sequentes terminos
$$n\,[n]\,x^n + (n-\alpha)[n-\alpha]\,x^n + (n-\beta)[n-\beta]\,x^n + (n-\gamma)[n-\gamma]\,x^n + \text{etc.}$$
Hi igitur termini $x^n$ utrinque debent poni aequales, unde erit
$$n\,[n] + (n-\alpha)[n-\alpha] + (n-\beta)[n-\beta] + (n-\gamma)[n-\gamma] + \text{etc.} =$$
$$\lambda\alpha[n-\alpha] + \lambda\beta[n-\beta] + \lambda\gamma[n-\gamma] + \lambda\delta[n-\delta] + \text{etc.}$$
unde conficitur
$$n\,[n] = {\lambda\alpha \atop -(n-\alpha)}[n-\alpha] {+\lambda\beta \atop -(n-\beta)}[n-\beta] {+\lambda\gamma \atop -(n-\gamma)}[n-\gamma] {+ \atop -}{\text{etc.} \atop \text{etc.}} \quad \text{Q. E. D.}$$

Corollarium. Cum in serie $P$ exponentes ipsius $x$ sint $0, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc., in serie $S = P^\lambda$ aliae potestates non occurrunt, nisi quarum exponentes sunt summa $\lambda$ terminorum hujus seriei $0, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc. unde si in hac serie $S$ omnes plane potestates ipsius $x$ occurrant, id erit indicio omnes plane numeros reduci posse ad summam $\lambda$ terminorum istius seriei $0, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc. At si quaepiam potestas $x^n$ non occurrat, tum ejus coëfficiens $[n]$ aequabitur nihilo. Manifestum autem est, nullum coëfficientem fieri posse negativum.

A. m. T. I. p. 335. 336.

items.quote:
Proposita serie potestatum quacunque
$$P = 1 + x^\alpha + x^\beta + x^\gamma + x^\delta + \text{etc.}$$
ejusque sumatur potestas exponentis $\lambda$, nempe $P^\lambda$, in qua evoluta occurrat terminus $[n]\,x^n$, ejus coëfficiens $[n]$ ita pendebit ab aliquibus praecedentium
items.english: Given any power series P = 1 + x^α + x^β + ..., if its λ-th power P^λ is expanded and contains the term [n]x^n, the coefficient [n] depends on some of the preceding ones so that n[n] = (λα − (n−α))[n−α] + (λβ − (n−β))[n−β] + ..., continued as long as n−α, n−β, ... are not negative.

items.quote: si in hac serie $S$ omnes plane potestates ipsius $x$ occurrant, id erit indicio omnes plane numeros reduci posse ad summam $\lambda$ terminorum istius seriei $0, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc.
items.english: If all powers of x occur in the series S, this indicates that every number can be reduced to a sum of λ terms of the series 0, α, β, γ, δ, etc.

items.quote: Manifestum autem est, nullum coëfficientem fieri posse negativum.
items.english: It is evident, however, that no coefficient can become negative.
